text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Tuesday:

- New York City started hearings about whether Swiss banks were holding dormant accoiunts of Holocaust victims. A spokesman of the city council said that the boycott threat should remain until Switzerland set up an 'adequate' fund.
- Swiss regional airline Crossair said it would axe a third of its flights from Lugano to Italian towns. By doing so, Crossair hopes to increase profitability.

- Large Swiss insurance, pharmaceutical and machinery companies plan to contribute to the 100 million Swiss franc fund, which has been created by the three largest Swiss banks to help Holocaust victims.
- American watch sellers plan to take legal steps against Swiss watch maker Swatch, saying Swatch has begun to set up its own shops near licenced Swatch shops.
- The Electronic Bourse Switzerland (EBS) still faces several technical problems. On Monday, the response time was so slow that some banks could not properly trade.

- The number of unemployed people in Switzerland rose by 13,330 to a record 205,501 in January. The unemployment rate went up from 5.3 to 5.7 percent. The canton of Ticino registered the highest rate in Switzerland with 9.2 percent.
- Swiss watch makers shipped products with a total value of 7.551 billion Swiss francs in 1996, down 1.6 percent from the previous year.
